title: OKDP platform values
description: The settings of global.okdp the OKDP compiler reads, given by the context's values layers, the platform's at level 0 (platform.yaml, Inputs.Context). Every compile checks them, in every mode, and reports every violation at once; it applies the defaults. Only the settings the compiler reads are described: any other key is allowed (a key the mappings read...) but certificateIssuers and serviceCatalog, former settings, refused (false): certificateIssuers' selfSigned.name is tls.clusterIssuer, serviceCatalog the menu of catalogs.yaml, beside platform.yaml. Every key reaches the mapping as written (global.okdp) and every chart (global). As in a chart's values, a null deletes a setting's default, and is refused where there is none; an empty string is a value. The whole of global.okdp is the platform's, level 0's: a layer above it, a project's (project.yaml), sets provisioning, its classes, and no other key, described here or not, whether the platform sets it or not; a project's own settings go under global beside okdp (global.project).

okdp.description: The platform's settings: level 0's, every key of it but provisioning, which a project adds its classes to.

tls.description: The platform's certificates, whichever cert-manager and trust tool run on the cluster: OKDP's or the cluster's own.

clusterIssuer.description: The cert-manager ClusterIssuer of the services' certificates (OKDP's self-signed CA, an ACME or a corporate one), which the mappings and the rule sets read. Absent: "".

caBundleSecret.description: The Secret of each namespace that holds the platform's CA bundle, ca.crt (PEM) and bundle.p12 (PKCS#12), as a trust-manager Bundle writes one, whichever tool fills it: the packages mount it to trust the platform's certificates. Absent: the platform's certificates are trusted without a bundle (public CAs).

charts.description: The upstream charts that render the charts the compiler adds itself, each a repository, a chart and its version. Each is checked after the requirements as a dependency of Chart.yaml is: a repository URL, the name of a chart, a pinned version.

objects.description: The chart of the instance's objects: a chart that renders its manifests value as written. Absent: oci://quay.io/okdp/charts, okdp-objects, 0.1.0.

repository.description: The URL of the chart repository: https:// or oci://; http://, the chart fetched in clear, is refused.

chart.description: The name of the chart in the repository.

version.description: A pinned version (1.2.3), not a range.

proxy.description: The platform's proxy: platform.proxyEnv, the environment variables of each setting that is not empty.

provisioning.description: The classes of the claims, by contract, as Kubernetes' storage classes: each class the provider of its claims and what it fixes of their request, one of them the default class, of the claims that name neither a class nor a provider. A claim names a class (class), or its provider (provider), or takes the default class; one that names neither, without a default class, is refused. The platform gives its classes and the default (platform.yaml); a project adds classes of its own (project.yaml), and the default of a contract the platform leaves without one, and changes none of the platform's: a class and a default are each taken whole. The platform's classes route every namespace to their providers; a project's reaches a provider of another namespace with its consent only, the claimers of the provider's instance.yaml, else of its package's provisions, listing the project. Never an instance.

default.description: The default class of the contract: a class of classes, the one of the claims that name neither a class nor a provider. Set once, at the lowest level that sets it: a project that wants another provider adds a class and names it.

classes.description: The classes of the contract, by name, a DNS-1123 label: another name is refused.

^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$.description: A class: the provider of its claims, and what it fixes of their request.

provider.description: The instance that provisions the claims of the class: <namespace>/<name>, or <name> of the claimer's namespace, the name the instance's name or its release. Of another namespace than the claimer's, it serves a class of the platform's (level 0), and a project's only when its claimers list the claimer's namespace, or *.

request.description: What the class fixes of the request of each of its claims, checked with it against the contract's claim schema (x-okdp-claim): a claim that sets one of its keys is refused.

secrets.description: The platform's secret store: where secrets go between namespaces, and where connections may keep their credentials.

store.description: The name of the secret store of External Secrets the credentials of a claim bound across namespaces go through: its provider pushes them (a PushSecret, deleted from the store with the claim), its claimers read them (an ExternalSecret), under the key <provider's namespace>/<claim ID>, the ID starting with the claimers' namespace, a property per secret field of the contract: a path-based store (OpenBao, Vault, a cloud secret manager) scopes a writer by the first segment and a reader by the first label of the second; the platform's own keys are under platform/, a namespace no project may have. Required by such a claim whose output has a secretRef. A connection whose secretRef is {remoteKey: <key>} keeps its credentials there, under that key: each instance that references it reads them (an ExternalSecret) into a Secret of its namespace, <release>.<connection>-credentials. Required by such a connection.

provider.description: The provider of the store, External Secrets' SecretStore spec.provider, verbatim (vault: an OpenBao or Vault server, its KV v2 mount, its Kubernetes auth, whose serviceAccountRef names serviceAccount). Set, the store is a SecretStore of that name in each project's namespace, which the targets write with the ServiceAccount serviceAccount, and the PushSecrets and ExternalSecrets reference it (kind SecretStore): the store's policy scopes each namespace by the identity it authenticates with. Unset, the store is a ClusterSecretStore of that name the platform created, one identity for every namespace: one trust domain.

serviceAccount.description: With provider: the ServiceAccount of each project's namespace the store authenticates with, the one provider's serviceAccountRef names.

refreshInterval.description: How often the PushSecrets push the credentials of the claims across namespaces to the store, and the ExternalSecrets read them, and those of the connections kept in it (refreshInterval, a duration): rotated credentials reach their claimers within it.

access.description: Who administers the platform, and how the Kubernetes API server names the identity provider's groups. A project's people are its file's (project.yaml access: the roles of groups within the project, okdp-project-<namespace> an editor by default), which the targets write as Argo CD roles of its AppProject and RoleBindings of its namespace. Another key is refused.

admins.description: The groups of the platform's administrators, as the identity provider's tokens give them (groups claim): bound once, by the platform's bootstrap, to Argo CD's role:admin and to the cluster's administration; the compiler writes nothing of them, a program that mirrors the platform's authority reads them (compiler.PlatformAdmins). Absent: none.

groupPrefix.description: The prefix the Kubernetes API server gives the groups of the users its tokens authenticate (the groups prefix of its token authenticator: its command-line flag, or the claimMappings of its structured authentication configuration): the RoleBindings of a project's groups name each group with it, k8s:okdp-project-demo for k8s:. Argo CD reads the groups claim as it is, without it. Absent: "", the groups as the tokens give them.

network.description: The network policy of the projects' namespaces. Another key is refused: a misspelt one would leave the namespaces open.

policy.description: true: the targets write, in each project's namespace but the platform's own (policy.privileged), a NetworkPolicy that denies every ingress to its pods but from the namespace itself, from ingressNamespaces and from the namespaces whose claims its instances provide; egress left open. false or absent: none, the namespaces open (the compiler does not know the cluster's ingress controller, nor whether its network plugin enforces policies).

ingressNamespaces.description: With policy: the namespaces whose pods reach every project's pods: the ingress controller's, a monitoring's. Absent: none, a project's services reached by its own namespace and its claimers only.

controlPlane.description: The optional control plane (okdp-control-plane-server). Absent: the platform has none, and the targets bind no identity of it. Another key is refused.

serviceAccount.description: The control plane's identity, its ServiceAccount: the targets bind it, in each project's namespace, privileged or not, to the Role okdp-control-plane, what it needs there and nothing more (docs/specs/01_inputs_outputs.md, the control plane's role); its ClusterRole keeps namespaces get and create.

ruleSets.description: The rule sets the platform requires: each by its name, core for the compiler's mandatory set, and optionally a constraint on its version (comparators separated by commas, each =, !=, >, >=, <, <=, ~ or ^ followed by a version MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, or a version alone). A compile that was not given a set listed, or of a version its constraint refuses, is refused: the settings a set reads would be read by none.

version.description: A constraint on the set's version; absent, any version.

policy.description: The platform's policy: what the projects may deploy, and which projects are the platform's own. Another key is refused: a misspelt one would leave the projects unconstrained.

privileged.description: The namespaces of the platform's own projects (cert-manager, an operator, a service mesh...), whose instances install cluster-scoped objects, write other namespaces and set any upstream value, as the other projects may not: the compile refuses their objects of a cluster-scoped kind or of another namespace; the targets give their releases the engine's own identity, the other projects' one confined to their namespace (Result.Privileged).

reserved.description: Namespaces no project may have, beside those of the rule set's namespace check: the namespaces of the platform's own components that are not projects of the tree (the secret store's, the identity provider's, the git server's, a CI runner's...). Every instance of such a project is refused, privileged or not: a namespace both lists is reserved.

projectApiGroups.description: API groups added to the Role a project's releases are installed with in its namespace (Flux, the rule set's document deployerRole): the groups of the custom resources a project's charts deploy beside those the standard set lists. RBAC has no negation: the Role lists its groups, and the groups of the deployer engines, or *, are never added, whatever this list says. A chart's Role of a group that is not added is refused by the API server (escalation).

projectGlobals.description: The keys of global the layers above level 0 set (a project's project.yaml, an instance's connections.yaml), beside okdp, which is the platform's: every chart of the instances receives global, past its package's protect, so any other key is refused (a field problem at global.<key>). Absent: project (a project's own settings, which its packages' mappings read) and storageClass; []: none. The list holds for every project, privileged or not. What the listed keys hold is the host's policy to check (Inputs.CheckGlobals), as the upstream values; level 0's global is the platform's, reviewed with it.
